commitResults.messageTitle: Show persisted parent-student links in storage diagram
commitResults.messageBody:
The DG storage class diagram shows JsonSerializableAddressBook owning
only JsonAdaptedPerson objects. The real class also owns a list of
JsonAdaptedLink objects, so readers cannot see where parent-student
links are saved or why a hand-edited link can stop a file loading.

Let's add JsonAdaptedLink to the diagram and regenerate the PNG.
Let's also note in the Storage section that each link is stored by
names and phone numbers, and that null, duplicate, or dangling links
are rejected on load.

commitResults.messageTitle: Align User Guide pictures with their descriptions
commitResults.messageBody:
Several UG pictures do not match the text beside them. The quick start
says the first launch shows an empty list, but its picture shows five
contacts from a Windows test run. The list and view sections reuse that
same picture, and the sort, link, unlink, find, and delete pictures
show commands that none of the listed examples use.

Let's capture an empty first-launch window, a list result, and a
view 2 result from the same sample contacts as the other pictures.
Let's also add the pictured command to each section's examples, and
change the sort example to the filter shown in its picture, so every
picture matches an example on the page.

The DG Acknowledgements list notable AI use for two members but not
for jingyucodes. The course policy on reuse asks each member to
acknowledge AI tools they relied on.

Let's add an entry in the same format, naming Claude Code and the
work it assisted with: the view, link, and unlink commands and tests,
alpha-bug fixes, UG/DG updates, v1.5 release preparation, and
pull-request reviews.
Update UI diagram with contact detail panel

commitResults.messageTitle: Repeat scroll and layout so tall rows settle after resizing
commitResults.messageBody:
After a resize, the list resets its skin and calls scrollTo once for
the selected contact. The new skin has not measured the wrapped cards
yet, so scrollTo positions rows using estimated heights. On Linux,
where fonts render taller, this left the last contact just below the
viewport, and the resize UI test failed under Xvfb.

Let's repeat scrollTo and layout a few times. Each layout pass
measures more of the real row heights, so the position settles with
the selected row inside the viewport.

commitResults.messageTitle: Keep selected contacts visible after resizing
commitResults.messageBody:
Resizing the contact workspace can move the selected row outside the
visible list as wrapped cards change height. The detail pane still shows
that contact, leaving the list and details visually disconnected.

Restore the selected row's scroll position after resized cells finish
layout. Keep the existing compact layout and selection behavior, limiting
the production change to 10 added lines during feature freeze.

long text, scrolling, command visibility, draft text, and keyboard focus.

commitResults.messageTitle: Wait for rendered contacts in resize UI tests
commitResults.messageBody:
Two layout pulses do not guarantee that native resizing and virtualized
row rendering have completed. Looking up the contact too early can fail
with an unhelpful NoSuchElementException on Ubuntu CI.

Wait for the expected rendered name with a bounded timeout and report
the viewport and visible cell indices on failure. Preserve the original
visibility checks; the test still fails without the production fix.

Center the final tag when checking detail scrolling so Linux font and
padding differences do not require the entire bottom padding to fit.
Keep the production change at 10 added lines during feature freeze.

commitResults.messageTitle: Include assertion details in test failure logs
commitResults.messageBody:
Short Gradle test output omits the assertion message and caller frames
needed to identify the headless resize failure in Ubuntu CI.

Log full test exceptions so viewport dimensions and rendered contact
indices are available when a regression fails. Keep test behavior and
application code unchanged.

commitResults.messageTitle: Reset contact row measurements after resizing
commitResults.messageBody:
On Ubuntu CI, shrinking the live window to 850x460 renders contacts 18
and 19 while leaving the selected contact 20 out of view. Waiting for
additional rendering does not restore the selected row.

Recreate the list skin before laying out and restoring the selected
contact's scroll position. This resets the cached row measurements that
refreshing the list alone leaves in place. Keep the production diff at
12 added lines during feature freeze.

Keep the regression's normal layout-pulse synchronization and useful
failure diagnostics. Preserve the tag-centering check for Linux fonts.

Run fresh CI after re-enabling the repository's Java workflow.

commitResults.messageTitle: Keep resized contact names readable in the viewport
commitResults.messageBody:
The resize regression accepts a name with only a few pixels inside the
outer list bounds, allowing an unreadable selected contact to pass.

Check the actual clipped viewport and require the first full text line
to fit. Reject nearly hidden names above and below the list, and reserve
enough height for a readable name in the stacked layout. This addresses
the clipping exposed by the stricter assertion at the smallest size.

Document the contact parameter used by revealContact as required by
the project's JavaDoc standard.

commitResults.messageBody:

These can mislead users transferring data and testers checking feedback,

Correct the invalid-load and delete test expectations. Distinguish

behavior without introducing functional changes during feature freeze.
